scope: Clarify the semantic roles that graph closure must distinguish for associative networks while assessing the unresolved AC1032 class-version-2 candidate.
supportClaimEffect: none; ObjectARX API semantics do not specify DWG class-version-2 serialized field layout or qualify output

authorities.title: Autodesk ObjectARX 2018 Developer Guide — Networks of Actions
observations: A network logically knows about its actions; an action may also be physically hard-owned by that network.
The database top-level ACDBASSOCNETWORK is under NOD key ACAD_ASSOCNETWORK through a subdictionary that soft-owns the network object.
Block-record subnetwork membership can be logical through the top-level network while physical ownership is through a block-record extension dictionary.

authorities.title: Autodesk ObjectARX 2022 Developer Guide — Main Concepts
observations: Associative networks organize actions as a directed acyclic graph and a network is itself an action.
Dependencies connect actions to objects/entities; the network keeps actions together and does not itself own those objects/entities.

keepDistinct: NOD key and dictionary ownership path to the top-level network
implementationImplication.sourceCandidate: The existing AC1032 example_2018.dwg receipt captures root 0x390 and child 0x38E with their dictionary owners, owning-network reference, action membership references, and separate base/network indexes.
implementationImplication.limitation: The Autodesk pages describe runtime/object-model semantics, not the class-version-2 DWG byte sequence. Keep m_networkFieldsParsed false and the AC1032 writer route refused until schema and producer evidence bind the physical fields.

nextAction: Use the distinct-role checklist when pursuing authoritative class-version-2 evidence and recursive source graph closure; do not reinterpret the existing candidate byte spans from API semantics alone.
